pr_title: statistics: skip reading mysql.stats_histograms if cached stats is up-to-date
pr_body:

### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/24096

Problem Summary:

There is no write in the cluster, while mysql.stats_histograms is repeatedly read.

### What is changed and how it works?

What's Changed:

Skip reading `mysql.stats_histograms`  if the cached stats is up-to-date.

### Related changes

N/A

Side effects

The test `(*testStatsSuite).TestVersion` failed.

Background:
https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/59b99ce1d4de338867a5f98c9d23ad1d6b3703e5/statistics/handle/handle.go#L837-L839
When loading stats, we only load columns/indexes which exist in the infoschema.

The test case is basically asserting that when infoschema in a tidb get updated (added a column in the test case) but stats in the tikv doesn't change (which means no `version` of the stats is changed), `(*Handle).Update(infoschema.InfoSchema)` should update the stats cache according to the changes of infoschema.

Before this PR, this is achieved by this redundant loading of stats that already has `version` up to date. But now it's removed in this PR.

I think changes in this PR are reasonable, but we still need to decide what's the correct behavior when scenarios similar to the test case happen.

issue_context.title: statistic load useless stats_histograms endlessly
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

Just create a table and then write a little data. 

Then see the `key visualizer` in `tidb dashboard`:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26020263/115035219-ee30f600-9efe-11eb-8d49-d380d5fec4b6.png)

As you can see, TiDB read the `stats_histograms` table endlessly. But the database doesn't do any operation.

So I just add some log in related code in TiDB:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26020263/115035587-4e279c80-9eff-11eb-9027-b99d37527aa0.png)

then, the related log output is:

```go
[2021/04/16 22:02:45.837 +08:00] [INFO] [handle.go:241] ["update -- 0"] [old-version=424293931453513741] [offset=2359296000]
[2021/04/16 22:02:45.837 +08:00] [INFO] [handle.go:247] ["update -- 1"] [last-version=424293929094217741]
[2021/04/16 22:02:45.838 +08:00] [INFO] [handle.go:262] ["update -- 2"] [last-version=424293931453513741] [table-id=62]
[2021/04/16 22:02:45.843 +08:00] [INFO] [handle.go:533] ["updateStatsCache -- "] [new-version=424293931453513741]
[2021/04/16 22:02:48.836 +08:00] [INFO] [handle.go:241] ["update -- 0"] [old-version=424293931453513741] [offset=2359296000]
[2021/04/16 22:02:48.836 +08:00] [INFO] [handle.go:247] ["update -- 1"] [last-version=424293929094217741]
[2021/04/16 22:02:48.838 +08:00] [INFO] [handle.go:262] ["update -- 2"] [last-version=424293931453513741] [table-id=62]
[2021/04/16 22:02:48.842 +08:00] [INFO] [handle.go:533] ["updateStatsCache -- "] [new-version=424293931453513741]
... 
... endless same upper log
...
```

As you can see, the `old-version` is always `424293931453513741`, and the `last-version` is always `424293931453513741`. **TiDB load useless `stats_histograms` endlessly.**

So why? After I check the code, I got it. But I don't understand why we need the chosen code block as below:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26020263/115036637-47e5f000-9f00-11eb-9e0d-53f64acf6ecb.png)

As you can see, the chosen code block causes the endlessly load `stats_histograms`.  

So why need the chosen code block?

### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)

<!-- Paste the output of SELECT tidb_version() -->
```sql
> select tidb_version()\G

***************************[ 1. row ]***************************
tidb_version() | Release Version: v4.0.0-beta.2-2658-g281d13465-dirty
Edition: Community
Git Commit Hash: 281d1346574cbc07d1e41f6428a5145a146dedfc
Git Branch: master
UTC Build Time: 2021-04-16 13:52:23
GoVersion: go1.15.6
Race Enabled: false
TiKV Min Version: v3.0.0-60965b006877ca7234adaced7890d7b029ed1306
Check Table Before Drop: false

```
comments: Same problem as https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/23406, i.e, there is no other stats operations that would push the `LastUpdateVersion` forward.

According to the code comment:

```
 235     // We need this because for two tables, the smaller version may write later than the one with larger version.
 236     // Consider the case that there are two tables A and B, their version and commit time is (A0, A1) and (B0, B1),
 237     // and A0 < B0 < B1 < A1. We will first read the stats of B, and update the lastVersion to B0, but we cannot read
 238     // the table stats of A0 if we read stats that greater than lastVersion which is B0.
 239     // We can read the stats if the diff between commit time and version is less than three lease.
```

The correct offset should be `mathutil.MaxInt64(int64(h.Lease()), int64(ddlLease))` now. To avoid the endless and redundant reading of `mysql.stats_histograms` if `LastUpdateVersion` is not increased, seems we should use `version > current_timestamp - offset` as the filter? @winoros @qw4990 how do you think?

Increasing the `offset` to be `ddlLease` may cause heavier reading of each `Update()`, since most of the records may have already been loaded.

https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/24175 can avoid the `stats_histograms` overhead, but the redundant read of `stats_meta` still exists unless we change the forward mechanism of `LastUpdateVersion`.
